description: "We are Westerhout 4, a multidisciplinary squad of coders, dreamers, and problem-solvers tackling the cosmos with open data. Armed with curiosity and caffeine, we're turning complex space and Earth science challenges into real, actionable solutions.
summary: ZERO-DRAFT is a mission-control style web dashboard that summarizes, ranks and interprets NASA's microgravity combustion investigations for spacecraft fire safety, built around the 129 BASS-II fire tests run on the ISS. It audits NASA's raw PSI-25 spreadsheet: 7 rows report impossible or missing oxygen, and we reproduce the arithmetic that produced them. It runs NASA's own published models live and ranks the investigations we indexed by relevance to crew habitat atmospheres. The Earth vs Orbit Burn Twin shows the core finding: a PMMA rod that goes out at 15.4% oxygen in 1g keeps burning to 13.61% in a gentle orbit airflow, by the report's Eq. 6.1. The cabin simulator shows a fire the size of Test M5 crossing the 1-hour CO limit in any sealed space under about 4.5 m³. An AI Lab Partner answers questions by running these models, and a script drops any sentence whose quote or number it can't trace. Every number on screen opens NASA's own words, with page numbers. It matters because lunar landers and rovers plan to use more oxygen at lower pressure, and no microgravity test of solid materials that we indexed covers that atmosphere.
details:
What it is

ZERO-DRAFT is a mission-control style dashboard that summarizes, ranks and interprets NASA's microgravity combustion investigations for spacecraft fire safety. It is for fire-safety engineers, mission designers and NASA's data curators: people who need the research digested and checkable, line by line.

How it works

Overview: the Earth vs Orbit Burn Twin. Drain the oxygen and a 1g flame goes out at 15.4% while the orbit flame, driven by the BASS-II report's Eq. 6.1, keeps burning to 13.61% at a gentle 2 cm/s airflow.

Summarize: all 129 BASS-II tests from NASA's raw PSI-25 spreadsheet, audited. A quarantine bay holds the 7 tests whose final oxygen is impossible or missing, and "Show the math" reproduces each value from NASA's Appendix A (for example 19.1 + 20.0 = 39.1%). A "Checked against NASA" panel puts our recomputed statistics, medians and means, beside the report's own numbers. We also list contradictions we found in NASA's PSI catalog records, such as Saffire-I's record carrying SAME's dates.

Rank: an Orbital Risk Index built only from measured BASS-II indicators, with its formula on screen and adjustable weights (labeled "not a NASA rating"); a flammability map; an ignition race against NASA Test 1's 25-second igniter; and a relevance ranking of the indexed investigations against target habitat atmospheres.

Interpret: a cabin fire, toxicity and nitrogen-dilution simulator built from the report's validated relations. Its five presets include a replay of Test M5, the same fire in a small sealed cabin (it crosses the 1-hour CO limit below about 4.5 m³), and a lunar 34% O2 / 8.2 psia case where the app refuses to predict, because no indexed microgravity test of solid materials covers that atmosphere.

Lab Partner: an AI assistant that answers questions by running the app's own models, visibly changing the views (with Undo), and citing a source for every sentence.

Why it matters

Earth screening tests miss how materials burn in orbit, and lunar landers and rovers plan to use more oxygen at lower pressure. ZERO-DRAFT shows where the evidence is, where it is missing, and where NASA's public data needs fixing before anyone builds on it.

What is new

An audit of NASA's raw data that reproduces the arithmetic behind each bad value; NASA's own models run live with their limits stated; and an AI that operates those models instead of just chatting, with every quote and number machine-checked.

How we kept it honest

Every scientific number comes from a verified quote, from the raw CSV through tested audit code, or from a tested function with cited inputs. A script confirms every quote is on its stated PDF page. Models state their limits and show "Outside tested range" beyond them. Drawings are labeled "Illustration", model outputs "Model". Alarms come only from model state.

Tools

React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Recharts, motion, MiniSearch, Vitest; serverless functions on Vercel; Groq and Google Gemini APIs.

Use of AI

The application code was written with Claude Code (Anthropic: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2) under our direction; we planned and reviewed with Claude. In the app, Lab Partner uses an LLM live (Groq, openai/gpt-oss-120b; Google Gemini as fallback), and its suggested questions' answers are cached LLM output. An offline pipeline used an LLM to read NASA's Appendix A test notes. Every AI-written element in the app is labeled ("AI-written, checked" or "AI-read from NASA's notes, quote checked"). Every AI quote must appear verbatim on its source page, and every number must trace to a tool result or verified quote, or the sentence is dropped. Every AI-generated data file records generated By, model and prompt Version. No AI-generated images, video or audio are used.
